[Paper] GRASPrune is a post-training structured pruning toolkit for decoder-only LLMs. It learns global gates over FFN intermediate channels and attention KV groups, projects them into budget-feasible hard masks, applies lightweight rescale compensation, and exports a dense pruned checkpoint. The code currently supports LLaMA-style and Qwen-style models, including `meta-llama/Llama-2-7b-hf` and `Qwen/Qwen3-8B`. ## Installation Python 3.10 is recommended. ``` pip install -r requirements.txt ``` ## Pruning Run commands from the repository root. ### LLaMA ``` python train.py \ --model-id meta-llama/Llama-2-7b-hf \ --model-family llama \ --device cuda:0 \ --keep-ratio 0.6 \ --epochs 4 \ --num-samples 512 ``` ### Qwen ``` python train.py \ --model-id Qwen/Qwen3-8B \ --model-family qwen \ --trust-remote-code \ --device cuda:0 \ --keep-ratio 0.8 \ --epochs 4 \ --num-samples 512 ``` If the model is not cached locally, add: Main options: - `--keep-ratio`: retained structural budget. - `--epochs`: number of gate-training epochs. - `--num-samples`: number of calibration sequences. - `--max-len`: calibration sequence length. - `--output-dir`: custom output directory. ## Outputs Checkpoints are saved under `outputs/` by default.
